A storage backup MUST state whether writers remain active or are quiesced. For a stop-during-backup policy, record which containers were running, stop the required writers, create the archive, and attempt to resume those containers after success, failure or timeout. Do not start containers that were already stopped. Reconcile incomplete resume attempts and preserve their failure evidence. A live file archive MUST NOT be labeled an application-consistent database backup.

methodology: Each criterion is a mandatory hosting outcome. Matrix breadth is expanded under its owning requirement and scores once. Acceptance scenarios and all matrix parents are binary release gates with zero extra weight.

Criteria were reviewed against the complete original R01-R68 text and the surrounding compatibility-ledger obligations. Full source rows and clause-review records remain in JSON. Compound runtime outcomes require the whole declared result, not a count of files, functions, commits or passing assertions.

Implementation presence records missing, partial or implemented. Evidence state records missing, partial, implemented, verified, evidence_unavailable or failed. Only verified contributes 1. Every other state contributes 0. A fully complete R requires all child criteria and applicable acceptance/matrix gates to pass.

R44 database rows duplicate the specification engine table and are cross-linked. The specification product-area table duplicates the ledger area inventory. Neither creates additional parent rows or points. Architecture/version, engine lifecycle, Compose raw/differential behavior, notification safety and extended infrastructure obligations are retained even when they are prose outside tables.

The denominator is a reviewed decomposition, not a mechanically discovered feature count. Source/inventory/hash checks establish integrity; independent specification review must assess whether all clauses are represented without duplicate outcomes.

Eligible hosting criteria alone define the primary denominator. Deferred Task-derived preview remains in the definition inventory with explicit deferred_task eligibility and zero current hosting weight. A hosting gate evaluates only eligible criteria; later Task claims need their own acceptance.

Parent criterion links and required gate dependencies are frozen with their own baseline digest. Passing a gate requires every eligible linked criterion and dependency gate plus a valid named combined acceptance receipt. A36 additionally requires all other A/matrix gates on the audited candidate.
scope_notes: R69-R102 and A38-A66 are excluded from the primary hosting denominator. R07 imports the minimum R81/R82 untrusted-hosting isolation prerequisite. R13/R15 import the R87-R92 hosting input, trust, reuse and evidence-safety clauses. R17 imports R85 human production authorization for agent-produced work. These references do not make full workspace functionality a prerequisite for trusted hosting.

R65 durable Task collaboration, goals/activity/workspace/checkpoint/checks/candidate/preview/budget/history UI is deferred. Direct navigation and hosting without a Task remain scored. R54 task-derived previews are conditional on a future Task implementation and are retained outside eligible hosting coverage.

R68/A36 agreement of schema, API, permissions, audit, UI, operational behavior and tests is an aggregate release gate. It earns no extra feature point. Published support profiles and measured limits remain independently scored outcomes.

Coolify client adapters are conditional release contracts. No endpoint/request/response/error/version inventory is declared, so their unresolved contract gate stays missing and outside the fixed hosting-feature denominator. No endpoint is invented and no empty inventory passes.

Native Go agent instead of upstream SSH-only management is an explicit implementation difference. Test-CA HTTPS does not establish production DNS/ACME. Linux arm64 qualification does not establish amd64 or a full architecture/version matrix. Trusted Docker does not establish hostile-workload isolation.
evidence_notes: The primary figure is a conservative evidence-verified lower bound at the pinned audit SHA. It is not the percentage of implementation completed: many bounded capabilities exist without retained, relevance-qualified acceptance for this exact outcome/profile. Missing evidence is not proof of missing code.

No broad R, A or full matrix row has complete combined evidence at the audited SHA. Historical accepted foundations are real bounded accomplishments, but cannot be summed into a full journey or percentage.

unresolved_client_contract.description: Unresolved conditional Coolify client contract: select exact endpoints, versions, request/response/error behavior, authorization and lifecycle outcomes before implementing or claiming an adapter. No endpoint inventory is declared. Contract selection and its tests remain a required gate for any future client-compatibility claim; zero selected endpoints is not a pass.

update_procedure: For evidence-only refresh, choose an exact clean candidate and update audit_sha plus scripts/parity_audit.py BASE together. Re-extract original source ranges/text at that candidate and compare changes. Preserve criterion IDs, outcome definitions and denominator. Update source-manifest hash constants if source ranges move, while preserving outcome definitions; any semantic scope change follows the separate scoring-version procedure.

Recheck each credited test subject and complete relevant source/test/config/tool/dependency inputs. Retain unchanged historical credit only with explicit relevance; affected or unknown evidence becomes unverified until rerun. Update embedded pass artifacts, exact tests, profile and limits.

For a true scope change, increment scoring_version and schema/history handling, record every added/removed criterion ID with reason, and publish old/new denominator. Update the calculator frozen inventory/manifest rules through review. Never silently reweight outcomes.

Regenerate the report with --write, run --check and --self-test, review specification and code hygiene at the same candidate, and commit the audit. No latest-main inference or automatic credit from passing-test counts is allowed.

R81. Qualified isolation profiles. Run untrusted code in a supported VM boundary, with an explicit host/kernel/backend/guest-image support matrix, patch/update policy and resource controls. Distinguish task, preview and production boundaries. Use disposable guest disks for ephemeral work and explicit bindings for retained data. Never claim that VM isolation makes arbitrary malicious code harmless. Native Mac, Windows and Linux implementations require their own tests. A WSL distribution alone is not a qualifying VM isolation boundary. GPU/host-device access needs a separate qualified profile. W13

scope_obligations.text: R82. Filesystem and network grants. Deny access to personal home directories, host management interfaces, host Docker sockets, personal SSH agents and private networks unless explicitly granted for the task. Enforce network policy outside the untrusted guest, including IPv4/IPv6, host/private/metadata ranges, proxy paths and address revalidation after DNS resolution. Grant specific destinations, ports and data mounts with modes and lifetimes. An ingress tunnel only exposes authorized services and must not become a general LAN route. Revocation behavior must be exercised.

scope_obligations.text: R85. Human production authorization. Agent-produced changes require an authorized human decision over the concrete production plan after required checks. Enforce this at the application boundary for UI, CLI, MCP, repository automation and webhooks. Agents cannot change protected deployment policy or replace trusted checks to authorize themselves. A reviewed merge may satisfy the human decision only under an explicit policy that binds the accepted source/artifact, required evidence and final target plan; an unrelated historical PR approval is insufficient. Content or target changes require a new decision.

scope_obligations.text: R87. Effective build inputs. Freeze a canonical build input manifest including effective context bytes after ignore rules, relevant named contexts, Dockerfile/frontend, target, platform, resolved base identities, builder/toolchain version, effective build settings, dependency material and output-affecting secret generations. Include submodule/LFS material where used. Retain source lineage separately from content equivalence. A live mutable checkout MUST NOT change while its candidate input is being captured without detection and retry.
scope_obligations.limits: Only minimum hosting safety/input/trust clauses are imported. Later Task/Workspace product behavior remains excluded.

scope_obligations.text: R88. Conservative artifact reuse. Reuse an existing authorized artifact only when the manifest and refresh policy establish eligibility, the artifact is available with its expected identity, and current policy permits it. Unknown mutable external inputs require a declared freshness bound or disable complete-artifact reuse. Freshness-based reuse does not prove those external inputs remained unchanged. A matching Git SHA is insufficient. Record why reuse was accepted or refused and retain original provenance. Force rebuild, mutable-input refresh and check rerun are separate operations.

scope_obligations.text: R89. Cache trust and transport. Qualify registry-backed build-result caching first. Scope read and write permissions separately by team/project/trust class. Untrusted contributions MUST NOT overwrite a protected cache reference or supply authoritative check results. Prefer immutable per-run exports and controlled shared-reference updates. Warn that caches can contain private build material and apply the same disclosure boundary as source. Distinguish shared layer results from builder-local compiler/package cache mounts. Cache eviction MUST NOT delete pinned releases or backups. W5, W6

scope_obligations.text: R90. Required checks and reuse. Every check result records its exact source/artifact subject, definition version, execution environment/platform, time, outcome and retained evidence. Trusted policy chooses mandatory checks. Agent-edited tests can be useful additional evidence but cannot silently redefine the deployment gate. Runtime checks must execute the release artifact. Reuse of successful checks requires matching source/artifact subjects, check-definition and trusted-policy versions, fixtures, relevant environment and freshness criteria. Security or policy changes may require re-verification without rebuilding.

Display verification coverage per supported platform. Do not infer native correctness on one platform from a result on another. Seal index-embedded attestations before approval of that index, or retain later evidence by immutable references without mutating the approved identity. scope_obligations.text: R92. Artifact availability and retention. Publish through authorized, bounded transfers with digest verification and explicit completion state. Candidate publication and deployment MUST NOT claim an artifact exists when required uploads failed. Protect artifacts referenced by retained releases, active deployments and required evidence, with separate cache and checkpoint policies. Reconcile registry/object-store retention and garbage collection. Report unavailable/corrupt artifacts and require a new build/approval where recovery changes their identity. Qualify any self-hosted storage/registry combination before advertising its guarantees.

dedup_family_review.boundary: Each R10 safety outcome covers all five declared realizations once. Provider/manual matrix gates test actual integrations and add zero points. Queued supersession and delayed overwrite of an active release are distinct failure paths.
Repository/API authentication and scoped checkout credentials differ from authenticating an inbound deployment event. GitLab signature and duplicate manual/GitHub trigger leaves were removed.

Executing builder/daemon instance identity differs from exact tool version. Artifact-to-source/platform/daemon receipt binding rejects substitution; merely recording those identities does not prove the rejection invariant. Immutable input capture differs from reporting effective settings. Registry tag/digest retention and Git immutable-receipt aggregates now link the source/output evidence already scored. Effective build settings link their frozen-input manifest. Per-strategy delivery leaves check that output actually arrives; platform/availability/pull preflight and digest/trust enforcement score once under their common contracts.

Generic resource rollback now links retained-release selection/restore/safety outcomes. Database start/stop/restart now links the same resource-action contracts, whose acceptance must cover declared resource kinds.

Persisting selected configuration through UI/API differs from initializing the actual engine process. Initialization is narrower than the removed create/operate umbrella. Readiness, private-network reachability, stable volume identity and meaningful data I/O are separate observable checks. Generic database-redeploy preservation links engine retention/data checks.

Encrypted storage, metadata authorization, rotation and purpose-bound consumer delivery have different observable boundaries. Generic build/runtime secret delivery links actual Git/registry/application/database consumers. External-provider login differs from enforcing scope and resolution/cache/invalidation behavior; the previous generic external-policy points remain removed. Engine rotation/binding updates link per-engine rotation checks.

source.text: R13. Build records and outputs. Record resolved source or workspace checkpoint, frozen build input manifest, platform, builder identity, logs, cache outcome and immutable output identities. Accept image tags as convenient inputs and record selected digests. Keep original build provenance when an artifact is reused. A deployment retry MUST not silently rebuild different contents. R87–R92 define input, trust and verification rules.

verified_criteria.outcome: Derive owned-volume metadata identity from immutable binding independently of display/audit metadata

source.text: R38. Storage identity. Record each binding's destination, Docker volume identity or canonical host path, mount destination, mode, ownership and resource references. Keep identity stable across rename, redeploy and agent replacement. Distinguish managed files, managed directories and pre-existing host files. Classify each storage object as platform-managed or externally owned. Importing or mounting an external object does not transfer ownership; any supported ownership transfer MUST be separate, authorized and auditable.
